title: Introduction of Licensed Public PMD-sharing Services in 2019
what_it_is: Introduction of Licensed Public PMD-sharing Services in 2019

sections.label: PMD-sharing regulation and sandbox licences
sections.summary: LTA is taking a cautious approach to regulating PMD-sharing, studying fire risks, charging and insurance, with sandbox licences for small-scale operations next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: PMD-sharing services will allow more Singaporeans to use PMDs as they will not need to own or carry them around.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Drawing on the lessons from regulating the bicycle-sharing industry, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) is taking a cautious approach to regulating the nascent PMD-sharing industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Key issues being studied include fire risks and charging issues, as well as the need for third-party liability insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: When licence applications commence next year, operators will be allowed to apply for sandbox licences for small-scale operations with limited fleet sizes.

sections.label: E-scooter registration regime
sections.summary: From January 2019, all e-scooters, whether privately owned or operated by PMD-sharing operators, will have identification stickers pasted on them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA will also be introducing an e-scooter registration regime from January 2019 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Under this regime, all e-scooters, regardless of whether they are owned by private individuals or PMD-sharing operators, will have identification stickers prominently pasted on them.

sections.label: Stricter penalties, speed limit, UL2272 standard
sections.summary: There will be stricter penalties for errant users, the footpath speed limit lowered from 15 km/h to 10 km/h, and the UL2272 standard implemented to reduce fire risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We also have stricter penalties for errant users.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We will also be lowering the speed limit on foot paths from 15 kilometres per hour (km/h) to 10 km/h.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: At the same time, we will be implementing the UL2272 standard to reduce fire risks of motorised PMDs.
